questions.question: Is the copay shown a firm amount, or does a disclaimer mark it as only an estimate?
questions.why: Booking sites often hide important billing caveats (like 'this is only an estimate') behind small info icons that require hovering to read.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to notice and investigate visual tooltips that contain crucial financial disclaimers about their out-of-pocket costs.
questions.check: Does an info icon or tooltip say the amount is an estimate?
questions.say_example: Small print behind an icon - the <$20> is only an estimate. The real bill can come out different.

questions.question: Is the credit card being charged immediately, or is it only being held on file to enforce the cancellation policy?
questions.why: Many booking platforms require a card on file but do not charge the copay until the visit, while others charge a deposit immediately.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses clarity on when their money will actually leave their account and whether the transaction is a hold or an immediate charge.
questions.check: Does the page say when the card is charged?
questions.say_example: Card is held, not charged - they bill at the visit

questions.question: Is the consultation fee the same on the summary, the payment page, and the confirmation?
questions.why: Checking that the fee stays exactly Rs. 290 across the booking summary, PayU gateway, and final appointment list ensures you aren't overcharged.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the financial security of personally confirming that no hidden fees were added during the payment transition.
questions.check: Is the fee the same on the summary, the payment page, and the confirmation?
questions.say_example: The fee grew on the way - <290> at the summary, <340> at the payment page. Stopping until we know why.

questions.question: Are you authorizing a credit card to be kept on file for future balances or no-show fees?
questions.why: Some practices require a credit card on file to secure the booking, which they can automatically charge for future copays, deductibles, or missed appointments.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses control over which of their financial accounts is exposed to automatic, unprompted future billing by the clinic.
questions.check: Does the page say the card is kept on file for future charges?
questions.say_example: Saving this card lets them charge it later too - no-shows, leftover bills. That's part of the deal here. Still OK?

questions.question: How are you required to pay the medical fee?

questions.question: Is your UPI ID verified so you can pay?
